A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same research work, with reliably matchable methods, equations, tables and figures. v3 includes supplementary sections S1–S10; v4 ends after its references and omits that supplement.

before.justification: v3 reports original LIBERO, physical-robot and LLaRA/VIMA attack experiments, including supplementary sensitivity analyses and failure cases.

after.justification: v4 retains original LIBERO attack results in Tables 1–2, physical-robot outcomes in Section 4.3, and diagnostic and defense experiments in Figure 5.

M1.justification: The UADA, UPA and TMA objectives, action representation and patch-optimization procedure in Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Omitted supplementary hyperparameters reduce documentation without establishing a change to the method.

E1.justification: The LLaRA black-box evaluation in the VIMA environment across difficulty levels L1–L4 disappears with Section S2 and Table S1. This removes a distinct evaluation environment. BridgeData V2, the four LIBERO suites and physical-robot experiments remain.

E2.justification: UMA, Random Noise and benign controls retain the same membership in corresponding LIBERO comparisons. LLaRA is the victim policy in the omitted VIMA experiment, rather than an additional competing attack method.

E3.justification: The supplementary protocols testing DoF1 targets of ±0.5 and ±1.0 and four UPA weight combinations are no longer reported. Retained evaluations preserve 10 tasks with 50 trials per LIBERO suite, FR/NAD metrics, the timeout rule and 100 physical trials. Missing implementation disclosures do not establish changes to these retained protocols.

E4.justification: v4 removes the LLaRA transfer analysis, nonzero-target TMA sensitivity tests, UPA weight ablation and additional trajectory/failure-case evidence in Sections S2, S4 and S7–S9. Figure 5's inner-loop, patch-size and four-defense analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report FR standard deviations across tasks and retain the same trial counts. Neither provides seed counts, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The omitted supplementary tables introduce no distinct uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v3 Tables 1–3 match v4 Tables 1a, 1b and 2 numerically, and Figures 1–6 retain their results. However, Tables S1–S3 disappear, removing LLaRA/VIMA outcomes, nonzero-target results such as 87.8% simulation AFR at −0.5, and UPA parameter-sweep results spanning 86.5–93.4%. Additional qualitative outcomes also disappear.

T1.justification: The action definitions, attack losses, NAD construction and transformation equations remain mathematically unchanged in Equations 1–10. The omitted supplement contains no additional formal assumptions, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: VLA vulnerability analysis, three attack objectives, adversarial patches and NAD. The introduction retains the 100% and 43% headline figures. Local wording changes do not alter the scientific scope of these claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.6 revises the training-bias hypothesis from a single robotic system to a narrow range of systems. v4 also loses Section S5's qualification about selecting benign-successful tasks and S10's camouflage/practicality discussion. Main mechanism explanations and the redundant-DoF caveat remain.

D1.justification: v4 omits Section S3's AdamW learning rate of 0.002, 2,000-iteration schedule, batch size 6, transformation bounds, default 5% patch, selected UPA weights and placement coordinates. Real-world task/selection details and the 224×224 input resolution also disappear. The direct code link is removed while the project-homepage link remains; actual code availability is not established to have changed.

R1.justification: v4 removes Section S1's entire positioning against conventional human–robot safety approaches, including pre-/post-collision interventions and their distinction from adversarial threats. Associated safety references and the AdamW reference disappear. The main VLA and adversarial-attack reviews remain.

P1.justification: The complete supplementary narrative, its S1–S10 structure and corresponding main-text pointers are removed. Retained prose receives localized editing, including a shorter abstract and repaired conclusion. The robot-setup paragraph moves within Section 4.2, and author-role notes and acknowledgements are added.

P2.justification: v3 Tables 1 and 2 become side-by-side panels of v4 Table 1 with clearer generation/evaluation captions; Table 3 becomes Table 2. Main figure artwork is retained with sizing and placement adjustments. All three supplementary tables and four supplementary figures are removed, substantially reducing the visual evidence.

improvement.justification: Although v4 improves some wording and table captions, it removes essential reproducibility settings, the LLaRA/VIMA transfer study, and nonzero-target and hyperparameter checks. The physical-result claim remains without its benign-successful task-selection qualification. These substantial losses in reproducibility and evidential support outweigh the limited presentation gains.
